summary: Full-extraction pass over 20 stored Vanuatu fiscal documents (IMF 2024 and 2025 Article IV reports; Ministry of Finance budget books 2025-2026, half-year updates 2019-2026, December Treasury monthly reports 2019, 2022, 2023, and Citizenship Office / Constitutional Agencies revenue reports 2019-2024H1). Adds budget targets, agency-level splits, IMF projections, quarterly and year-to-date collections, and percent-of-revenue figures for the citizenship programmes.

events.title: Ireland ends visa-free travel for Vanuatu passport holders
events.description: IMF: financial-integrity risks of the ECP shown by the UK revoking visa-free travel in August 2023 and Ireland in March 2024; the EU to reinstate visa requirements permanently from February 2025.
events.quote: Risks to financial integrity posed by the ECP are highlighted by the decision to revoke visa free travel by UK in August 2023 and Ireland in March 2024.

gaps: Revenue reports by agency (Citizenship Office / Constitutional Agencies) exist in the store only for 2019-2023 and 2024 H1; full-year 2024 and later agency reports were not among the documents.

December Treasury monthly reports for 2019, 2022 and 2023 give December-month programme receipts only for 2019 and 2023; the 2022 report names the programme as a reason for December revenue but prints no December figure.
Charts in all documents (quarterly budget vs actual, IMF fiscal and BoP figures, DSA scenario charts) have no printed values.

ledger.contains: IMF 2024 Article IV staff report (CR 24/278, 94 pages). In scope: press release and key issues (declining ECP proceeds, words); para 10 (ECP projected revenue 60% below the authorities' 2024 target, partly from reactivation of a cheaper programme: a ratio to a target, no indicator, not taken; EU permanent visa removal from February 2025; event already recorded); para 14 (ECP revenue to average about 2.5% of GDP from a peak of about 14% in 2020: the 14 is a rounded restatement of the Table 3 value for 2020, already recorded, not added again); para 19 and 25 (authorities blame AML/CFT payment-clearance delays and an older, cheaper programme; considering keeping a higher share of fees now paid to agents; words); para 26 and footnote 29 (UK revoked visa-free travel August 2023, Ireland March 2024, EU full suspension February 2025; EU governance concerns); Table 2 and Table 3 ECP revenue 2020-2029 in vatu and percent of GDP; Table 5 balance of payments "ECP Revenues" (same percent-of-GDP series as Table 3, not added again); risk matrix (ECP 33% of total revenue in 2020, already recorded); Annex VII fiscal framework and DSA text (ECP around 14% of GDP in 2020 and 5.4% in 2023, restatements of table values; medium-term average 2.5%); DSA zero-ECP scenario tables and charts (debt ratios under a hypothetical scenario, not programme numbers, not taken); Executive Director statement (ECP once up to 14% of GDP; compositional shift to a lower-priced sub-programme, words). Charts (Figure 3, text figures) have no printed values; image pages 50, 56, 62, 63, 66 and 68 OCR-checked (no programme numbers). Rest is macro, financial, airline and climate material. Added: 2025-2029 projections (vatu and % of GDP), medium-term average, Ireland visa event.

IMF 2025 Article IV staff report (CR 25/277, 97 pages). In scope: press release and key issues (ECP revenues significant but in structural decline, words); 2024 fiscal outturn (ECP revenues stronger than expected, words); para 10 and footnote 8 (CIIP suspended March 2025, amended May 2025, resumed June 2025; ECP about 7% of GDP in 2024, down from 14% in 2020; events and the 7% already recorded); para 16 and footnotes 16-17 (H1 2025 ECP increase linked to invoicing, receipts still to be verified; Commission of Inquiry report; events already recorded); para 24 and footnote 25 (AML/CFT risks and EU governance concerns, words); authorities' views (words); Table 2 and Table 3 ECP revenue 2021-2030 in vatu and percent of GDP; balance-of-payments table "ECP Revenues" (same percent-of-GDP series, not added again); risk matrix (words); DSA zero-ECP scenario text, tables and charts (debt ratios under a hypothetical scenario, OCR-read from image pages 84-93; not programme numbers, not taken). Image pages 5, 36, 54, 57, 64, 66, 94 and 97 OCR-checked (no programme numbers). Rest is macro, labour migration, climate, banking and airline material. Added: 2026-2030 projections (vatu and % of GDP) and the 2020 "high of 14 percent".

Budget 2025 Volume 1, Fiscal Strategy Report (75 pages): economic outlook, summary fiscal position, 2024 fiscal performance (VDSP, VCP and CIIP collected VT 9,399.2m vs budget VT 10,983.8m, 12.0% above 2023's VT 8,399.1m), 2025 revenue estimates (Honorary Citizenship Program to fall 30.5% from VT 10,983.8m to VT 7,629.5m), revenue policy (citizenship programme declining 2023-2024; recommendations to align CIIP fees with the VDSP, review the 50% fee retention as investment funds, fewer sub-agents, more VDSP agents registered for VAT: policy proposals, no amounts, not tabled), IMF DSA with a zero-ECP scenario and debt chart (words; no printed values), Table 11 Citizenship Commission appropriation 2025-2029, Table 19 supplementary appropriation 2024 for Citizenship Commission staff recruitment. GFS tables (Tables 8-10) and debt tables (pages 28, 31, 64 are images, OCR-checked) have no separate citizenship line. Out of scope: all other fiscal and economic figures. Ratio 85.6% of budget not taken. Programme levels for 2023-2025 were already recorded.

Budget 2026 Volume 1, Fiscal Strategy Report (76 pages): economic outlook, summary fiscal position, 2025 fiscal performance to end-August (VDSP, VCP and CIIP VT 10,303.0m, 135.0% of the VT 7,629.5m budget, 96.4% above Jan-Aug 2024; footnote on direct invoicing from May 2025), 2026 revenue estimates (programme up 62.2% to VT 12,374.7m), revenue measures (Government relies on citizenship revenue; standardised payment procedure), economic update (revenue 37% of budget by April 2025, total revenue not programme), IMF DSA zero-ECP scenario (Chart 3, no printed values), budget policy statement text with the 2025 projection cut from VT 10 billion to VT 7 billion, Table 11 Citizenship Commission appropriation 2026-2030. GFS and debt tables have no separate citizenship line; Annex 1 (2025 supplementary appropriations) has no Citizenship item. Image pages 2, 54 and 76 OCR-checked (no programme content). Out of scope: other fiscal and economic figures. Ratio 135.0% of budget not taken. The 2026 budget was already recorded.

Constitutional Agencies revenue report 2020 (6 pages): agency shares of the revised budget (Citizenship Office 98.4%), year-end budget vs actual by agency (Table 3.1) and by revenue line (annex: Citizenship Office lines for CIIP fees, VERP honorary fees, Honorary Citizenship Program Fees, Other Fees, Application Charges Recoveries; State Law Office line Honorary Citizenship Program Fees = FIU due diligence fees), VDSP/VCP budgeted at 30.6% of the revised national revenue budget, 96.8% of State Law Office revenue from due diligence fees (a share of an agency's revenue; no fitting indicator, not taken), Citizenship Office 95.1% of Constitutional Agencies collections (agency share, not taken). Two charts without printed values. Other agencies (Judiciary, Parliament, Public Service Commission, Public Solicitor, other State Law Office lines) are out of scope. CIIP, VERP and honorary fee actuals were already recorded; budgets, office total and small fee lines added (CIIP and VERP budgets are printed as "-").

Constitutional Agencies revenue report 2021 (7 pages): agency shares of revenue (Citizenship Office 97.2%), year-end budget vs actual by agency (Table 3.1) and by line (annex: Citizenship Office two lines labelled Honorary Citizenship Program Fees, empty VERP line, Other Fees, Application Charges Recoveries; State Law Office Honorary Citizenship Program Fees = FIU due diligence fees); VDSP/VCP budgeted at 30.6% of national revenue; text misattributes the Constitutional Agencies totals (VT 11,604.5m budget, VT 12,709.8m actual) to the Citizenship Office (not recorded as programme figures); Citizenship Office 93% of collections and State Law Office 185% over budget (agency percentages, not taken). Three charts without printed values. Other agencies out of scope. Honorary fee actuals already recorded.

Constitutional Agencies revenue report 2022 (7 pages): agency budgets and shares (Table 1.1), year-end budget vs actual by agency with percent collected (Table 3.1) and by account line (annex: Citizenship Office Honorary Citizenship Program Fees, Other Fees, Citizenship Fees, Application Charges Recoveries, Inspections Recoveries; State Law Office Honorary Citizenship Program Fees = FIU due diligence fees); VDSP/VCP budgeted at 28% of national revenue; percent-of-budget-collected columns and agency shares (computed ratios, not taken); Inspections Recoveries 14,348 (a recovery, not a fee; sign unclear in the layout) not taken. One chart without printed values. Other agencies out of scope. Honorary fee actuals already recorded.

Constitutional Agencies revenue report 2023 (8 pages): agency budgets and shares (Table 1.1), year-end budget vs actual by agency (Table 3.1) and by account line (annex: Citizenship Office CIIP fees, Honorary Citizenship Program Fees, Other Fees, Citizenship Fees, Application Charges Recoveries; State Law Office/Attorney General Honorary Citizenship Program Fees and CIIP fees = FIU due diligence); VDSP/VCP budgeted at 26% of national revenue; text misattributes Constitutional Agencies totals (VT 9,118.9m / 8,072.6m) to the Citizenship Office (not recorded); 99.3% and 96.8% agency-share statements and percent-collected columns (computed ratios, not taken). Two charts without printed values. Other agencies out of scope. CIIP and honorary actuals already recorded; office totals, budgets, small fee lines and the State Law Office CIIP fee line added.

Constitutional Agencies half-year report 2024 (6 pages): agency shares (Table 1), half-year budget vs actual by agency (Table 2) and by line with full-year 2024 budgets (annex: Citizenship Office Honorary Citizenship Program Fees, Other Fees (no collections), Citizenship Fees, Application Charges Recoveries, CIIP fees; State Law Office/Attorney General Honorary Citizenship Program Fees and CIIP fees); VDSP, VCP and CIIP expected to bring 22.7% of 2024 national revenue; reasons for decline (EU visa waiver, correspondent banking, cheaper CIIP; event already recorded from the IMF); Attorney General revenue "VT 276 million" in text (conflicts with the table's 119.8m; agency total, not programme, not taken); percent-collected columns (computed, not taken). One chart without printed values. Other agencies out of scope. Citizenship Office honorary and CIIP actuals already recorded.

Citizenship Office 2019 revenue report (4 pages): cumulative quarterly budget vs actual for the Office (Q1-Q4), full-year table by item (Honorary Citizenship Program Fees = VDSP and VCP, Other Fees, Application Charges Recoveries) with budget, actual, variance, repeated in an annex with a different budget for the programme fees; VDSP/VCP budgeted at 22.8% of revised national revenue; collections 24.5% above 2018; overall 88.8% above budget (a variance percentage, no indicator, not taken); outstanding Citizenship Office receivables VT 131,745 at end-2019 (arrears of the agency, no fitting indicator, not taken); two charts without printed values (shown in the quarterly table). Full-year honorary fees actual was already recorded. All three printed budgets for the Office are recorded separately because they disagree.

Half-Year Economic and Fiscal Update 2019 (24 pages): global and domestic economic outlook, sector growth, inflation, balance of payments, exchange rate, fiscal update (revenue by tax and the VDSP/VCP paragraph: H1 2019 collections, revised budget, H1 2018 comparison and change; 2018 collections 371.5% above budget and above VAT for the first time), expenditure, financing, debt, revenue policy, and GFS tables. GFS statements of government operations (excluding and including donors, half-year and multi-year) show citizenship revenue only inside "Other revenue", not separately. Out of scope: all non-programme figures. Ratios to budget (82.5%, 371.5%) not taken. H1 2019 collections and the 2018 VAT event were already recorded.

Half-Year Economic and Fiscal Update 2020 (27 pages): economic outlook (COVID-19, Cyclone Harold), balance of payments (citizenship revenue as main government revenue from abroad, words only), fiscal update (VDSP/VCP H1 2020 collections, revised budget, H1 2019 comparison, change; programme receipts "over double the forecast" in each of the first three months, words, not taken), expenditure, debt, revenue policy, GFS tables. GFS statements of government operations (excluding and including donors, half-year and multi-year) show citizenship revenue only inside "Other revenue", not separately. Out of scope: non-programme figures. The 77.8% of budget ratio not taken. H1 2020 collections already recorded.

Half-Year Economic and Fiscal Update 2021 (24 pages): economic outlook, balance of payments (citizenship programme inflows, words), fiscal update (VDSP/VCP H1 2021 collections, budget, H1 2020 comparison and change; collections on average 13.2% above monthly forecast in H1 and footnote that the Government budgets programme revenue low on purpose; correspondent banking problems with the National Australia Bank), revenue policy (VDSP future at risk from correspondent banking; REO approved by Parliament in 2021 with unproven revenue potential; events already recorded), debt (shortfall in programme revenue, words), GFS tables. GFS statements of government operations (excluding and including donors, half-year and multi-year) show citizenship revenue only inside "Other revenue", not separately. Out of scope: non-programme figures. Ratios to budget/forecast (48.9%, 13.2% above forecast) not taken. H1 2021 collections already recorded.

Half-Year Economic and Fiscal Update 2022 (27 pages): economic outlook, real estate sector (REO not yet implemented), fiscal update (VDSP/VCP H1 2022 collections, budget, H1 2021 comparison and change; honorary citizenship programmes below budget), revenue policy (pressures on the programmes: correspondent banking 2021, EU visa waiver suspension, end of Change of Name policy; REO low revenue potential; plan to work with FIU and Citizenship Office on reforms; context event already recorded), debt tables, and GFS Tables 7-12 printed as images (OCR read: citizenship revenue not shown separately, only "Other revenue"). Out of scope: non-programme figures. The 48.7% of budget ratio not taken. H1 2022 collections already recorded.

Half-Year Economic and Fiscal Update 2024 (24 pages): economic outlook, fiscal update (VDSP, VCP and CIIP June 2024 and H1 collections, forecast, budget, H1 2023 comparison and change), revenue policy (citizenship revenue declining in 2023 and 2024; policies under review), public debt (programme revenue decline; Figure 2 debt scenario if the ECP is lost entirely: chart without printed values; UK visa-free suspension affected new applications, words), Table 5 debt targets (not programme), GFS tables. GFS statements of government operations (excluding and including donors, half-year and multi-year) show citizenship revenue only inside "Other revenue", not separately. Out of scope: non-programme figures. Ratios to forecast/budget (22.4%, 30.7%) not taken. H1 2024 collections already recorded.

Half-Year Economic and Fiscal Update 2025 (21 pages): economic outlook, balance of payments (citizenship-related revenue in secondary income, words), fiscal update (June 2025 revenue above forecast due to citizenship fees; VDSP, VCP and CIIP June and H1 collections, forecast, budget, H1 2024 comparison and change; footnote on direct invoicing of agents from May 2025), revenue policy (2025 budget VT 7,729.7m vs 2024 VT 11,303.8m; reforms incl. CIIP investment requirements and invoicing; collections VT 9,123.2m), GFS tables. GFS statements of government operations (excluding and including donors, half-year and multi-year) show citizenship revenue only inside "Other revenue", not separately. Out of scope: non-programme figures. Ratios to forecast/budget (239.8%, 123.4%) not taken. The invoicing event, 2024 and 2025 budgets and H1 total were already recorded.

Half-Year Economic and Fiscal Update 2026 (21 pages): economic outlook (professional services upgraded on demand from the economic citizenship programme, words), fiscal update (June 2026 revenue below forecast due to lower citizenship fees; VDSP, VCP and CIIP June and H1 collections, forecast, budget, H1 2025 comparison and change), revenue policy (2026 programme budget raised; reforms: compliance, agent management, stronger CIIP investment requirements, full invoicing; collections likely to exceed the 2026 forecast, words), GFS Tables 6-11 printed as images (OCR read: citizenship revenue not shown separately, only "Other revenue"). Out of scope: non-programme figures. Ratios to forecast/budget (47.8%, 71.1%) not taken. H1 2026 collections and the 2026 budget were already recorded.

Treasury monthly budget report, December 2019 (9 pages): summary of government operations, revenue by main tax and the VDSP/VCP paragraph (December collections and forecast, full-year 2019 total, revised budget, 2018 comparison, percentage differences), expenses with overspending items, financing and donor grants, terminology, charts without printed values, and GFS statements (Annexes 3-5) by month in which citizenship revenue is not shown separately (only within "Other revenue"). Out of scope: all non-programme fiscal figures. Percent-of-budget statements (65.5% above forecast, 93.1% above budget) are ratios to a budget and not taken; the 2019, 2018 and budget levels were already recorded.

Treasury monthly budget report, December 2022 (9 pages): government revenue, taxes, budget support, other revenue (VT 10,378.2m, mostly fees and charges) with the Honorary Citizenship Programs (VDSP and VCP) paragraph: 2022 collections, budget, 2021 comparison and percentage change; expenses, financing, charts without printed values, GFS statements by month without a separate citizenship line. December-month programme receipts are not printed (only named as a reason revenue beat forecast). Out of scope: non-programme fiscal figures. The 87.8% of budget ratio is not taken; levels were already recorded.

Treasury monthly budget report, December 2023 (9 pages): summary table, revenue by tax, budget support, VDSP/VCP paragraph (December collections and forecast, 2023 total, budget, 2022 comparison, percentage changes); December revenue shortfall attributed to lower Honorary Citizenship Program Fees; expenses, financing, charts without printed values, GFS statements by month without a separate citizenship line. Out of scope: non-programme fiscal figures. Ratios to budget (70.2% below forecast, 89.0% of budget) not taken; annual levels were already recorded.
